entries.claim_or_gap: A white swing makes more distribution calls than the damage roll, the outcome roll and the block-crit roll: CalcSpellResistedDamage rand_norm() for a magic-school weapon, DealDamage durability roll_chance(float RATE_DURABILITY_LOSS_DAMAGE, default 0.5) once for a player victim and once for a player attacker when damage > 0 and the victim survives (each followed by urand(0, EQUIPMENT_SLOT_END-1) on success), the creature daze roll and the item/aura proc rolls. Engine-output consumption per call is not modelled (uniform_int_distribution may reject). A stream-exact replay of Trinity's SFMT RNG is therefore unresolved; the per-swing outcome probabilities are unaffected.
entries.reopen_condition: a requirement to reproduce Trinity's RNG stream exactly; then model every call site above with the host's World.conf rates and libstdc++'s distribution algorithms

entries.claim_or_gap: weapon-sources.json listed 296087 (SkillLineAbility 40461, skill 840, AcquireMethod 0) as a dual-wield grant for specs 71/72/73, so `weapon`, the Track C hook and witnesses-c reported dual_wield=true for Arms and Protection. Fixed: AcquireMethod-0 class-line grants now sit in capability_by_spec_learned_only and count only when the caller supplies the spell as learned (--learned-spell / identity.learned_spells). Arms/Protection dual wield is character state.
entries.reopen_condition: a Trinity consumer or snapshot data source that teaches 296087/296088 automatically, or a fixture that supplies learned spells

entries.claim_or_gap: tmp = attackerLevel - victimLevel * 1000 - 1500 is int32 arithmetic on uint8 levels (<= 255), so tmp < 0 for every attacker type; because every earlier band that was added failed roll < sum, roll >= sum holds on entry and roll < sum + tmp is false. Crushing is dead code for creatures as well as players and pets, independent of data.
entries.reopen_condition: an upstream change to Unit.cpp:2489 (e.g. (attackerLevel - victimLevel) * 1000 + 1500) together with a creature >= victim + 4

entries.claim_or_gap: Hit (31), expertise (37), armor penetration (44) and block (15) rating are absent from every ItemSparse row and every SpellItemEnchantment stat effect; dodge (13) / parry (14) survive only on 1,785 legacy items (ExpansionID <= 10; one of each at ExpansionID 10), on 375 legacy enchants (IDs <= 5260, MaxLevel <= 35) and in the legacy bonus lists 6676 (block) / 6677 (dodge), none of which the current gear corpus uses. The §10 verdicts previously rested on the 7,812 ExpansionID-11 items only.
entries.reopen_condition: a current item, bonus list, gem or enchant carrying stat 13/14/15/31/37/44, or a MOD_RATING aura in scope with bit 5-7, 2-4, 23 or 24

entries.claim_or_gap: Whenever the chance path selects glancing (attacker GetLevelForTarget + 3 < victim GetLevelForTarget), the damage path's raw levels give leveldif >= 4, because a scalable creature's raw level is ScalingLevelMax + delta (Creature.cpp:1618) >= its GetLevelForTarget. leveldif is therefore capped to 3 and the factor is 1.f - 3*0.1f = 0.69999999f (1000 -> 700, probe). The negative-leveldif CleanDamage wrap is unreachable from that path.
entries.reopen_condition: a script or path that sets a creature's raw level below its GetLevelForTarget (Creature::SetLevel after SelectLevel), or a player attacker whose GetLevel differs from the level the victim scales to

entries.claim_or_gap: The 'MH and OH never swing in the same update' rule holds for DoMeleeAttackIfReady only. Queued extra attacks are drained earlier in the same Unit::Update as BASE_ATTACK swings without touching timers, so an extra MH swing and a regular OH swing can share an update.
entries.reopen_condition: a reachable SPELL_EFFECT_ADD_EXTRA_ATTACKS spell in scope (0 today; 28 in the catalog)

entries.claim_or_gap: CalculatePct<uint32,float>(base, 30) = uint32(base * 30.0f / 100.0f) first differs from the binary64 result at base 2,236,990 (671,096 vs 671,097; compiled tc_weapon_probe `pct` and a binary32 emulation agree). 16,777,219 is a discriminating value, not the lower bound, and not every larger base discriminates. Whether a white-swing or weapon-special amount fed to a 30 % CalculatePct (creature block, crit AddPct) reaches the millions in current content is not established.
entries.reopen_condition: a damage-magnitude census showing a CalculatePct input at or above 2,236,990 in current content, or a Trinity change of the template to double

entries.claim_or_gap: Every current-season item (ItemSparse.ExpansionID 11) resolves to required level 90 through ItemBonus 49 SCALING_CONFIG_AND_REQ_LEVEL (ItemScalingConfig 219/318 RequiredLevel 90). Player::CanUseItem refuses it below level 90 and _LoadInventory mails it, so the original level-80 fixtures were not loadable in Trinity although the compiler reported validation.ok. Fixed: the compiler checks the required level, and the synthetic fixtures are level 90. Items with a RequiredLevelCurve or a fixed scaling level are still reported unresolved (gearing does not evaluate them).
entries.reopen_condition: gearing evaluates RequiredLevelCurve / ITEM_MODIFIER_TIMEWALKER_LEVEL, or a fixture item carries ItemBonus type 27 or 13

entries.claim_or_gap: /derived/controlled_units correctly fails closed: controlled_units.ownership has no CHARACTER_PREP_HOOK, and call_hook records the miss. The hook would need to accept context {fixture, identity (+learned_spells), gear, spells, stats (null when unresolved), section, snapshot_build, trinitycore_commit} and return a dict with evidence_class, validate the section (hunter_pet creature_family_id / pet_specialization_id, active_demon summon_spell_id), and derive the pet level, stats and spells. Two identity values were verified (db2-fact): ChrSpecialization 74 = Ferocity (ClassID 0) and SpellName 30146 = Summon Felguard (acquired by the Demonology fixture).
entries.reopen_condition: Track A exposes CHARACTER_PREP_HOOK(context) -> dict

entries.claim_or_gap: The fixture format now has an optional identity section learned_spells (character_spell rows, Player::_LoadSpells -> AddSpell). The compiler roots those spells as learned-spell and passes them to the weapon hook. Class skill lines hold 3,789 AcquireMethod-0 'Learned' abilities (3,702 in the snapshot, 36 passive), which no automatic path teaches. Which of them a Retail character knows is character state. Not modelled: the active/disabled flags of character_spell and the spell_learn_spell dependents (5 world rows).

The 686 glyph spells carry aura effects that are not all cosmetic: SPELL_AURA_DUMMY x103, OVERRIDE_SPELL_VISUAL x26, aura 332 x6, PROC_TRIGGER_SPELL x5, ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER x5, aura 285 x3, and others. The fixture format has no glyph section and the compiler applies none.

entries.claim_or_gap: Player::_LoadSkills restores the saved skills of any SkillRaceClassInfo availability and runs LearnSkillRewardedSpells with the saved values. LearnDefaultSkills then skips those skills. The compiler assumes default-skill values only. Items with a RequiredSkill that is not a default skill are reported unresolved. The fixture format has no saved-skill section.
entries.reopen_condition: a saved-skill section in the fixture format, plus a census of AcquireMethod 1/2 combat spells on non-default skill lines (professions, riding, Availability-2 rows)

entries.claim_or_gap: Of the AcquireMethod-4 default-skill spells in the fixtures, 54197 and 50977 have no ShowFutureSpellPlayerConditionID, and the pinned TDB has no conditions row of source type 35 for their abilities (14 such rows exist, none for them). Trinity therefore learns them. The rest (e.g. 163201, 2645, 783, 697, 2006, 322109) and 121128 (a type-56 conditions row) depend on PlayerCondition 83446: Flags 0x21, ContentTuning 958, and ModifierTree 143919 = not on maps 2175/2236/2261/2369. That makes them depend on host location and level. The compiler keeps all of them unresolved and names the reason.
entries.reopen_condition: the conditions table becomes a compiler input, and a host-location input for PlayerCondition 83446

entries.claim_or_gap: 'Health starts full at the prepared maximum' is an encounter convention, not a Trinity construction path. Player::Create fills health before gear is applied, Unit::SetMaxHealth never refills, and LoadFromDB restores the saved value. Only GiveLevel fills after UpdateAllStats. The compiled evidence class was lowered to structural-inference.
entries.reopen_condition: a host specification of the encounter start state
